evidence.title: Model Context Protocol 2025-11-25 — Tools
supports: tool input and result validation guidance
evidence.notes: Supports protocol fields only; NetSpout audit and scenario metadata are explicitly separate.

evidence.title: Model Context Protocol 2025-11-25 — Resources and Prompts
evidence.notes: Prompt interactions are modeled only where the official protocol defines prompts/list and prompts/get.

evidence.title: Model Context Protocol 2025-11-25 — Authorization
supports: resource indicators, PKCE, and audience validation
evidence.notes: Authorization decisions are instrumentation audit evidence and are not invented MCP message fields.

evidence.title: Agent2Agent Protocol Specification
supports: Agent Card, Task, Message, Part, Artifact
taskId, contextId, status and update events
evidence.notes: Authorization remains implementation-specific after authentication; an exchange does not prove malicious intent.

evidence.title: OWASP Agentic AI Threats and Mitigations
supports: prompt injection, tool misuse, identity and delegation threat modeling
least privilege and external authorization controls
evidence.notes: Threat taxonomy support does not establish standards compliance.

evidence.title: SLSA v1.1 Provenance
evidence.notes: Missing provenance is modeled as a validation gap, never automatic proof of malicious activity.

evidence.title: NetSpout Phase 12 deterministic audit runtime
supports: secret redaction, fail-closed endpoint and payload policy
evidence.notes: Runtime evidence is NetSpout-defined and does not validate an external MCP, A2A, repository, registry, or CI implementation.

references.title: Indirect Prompt Injection
references.threat: A lower-trust artifact attempts to redirect an authorized agent task.
references.boundary: Untrusted artifact to agent planning context
references.simple: An untrusted document asks the agent to ignore its assigned job.
references.advanced: Correlate artifact provenance, policy evaluation, agent decision, and attempted tool use without treating the instruction as a compromise.

references.title: Unauthorized Tool Invocation
references.threat: An agent requests a capability outside its assigned permissions.
references.boundary: Agent runtime to tool authorization service
references.simple: The agent asks for a tool it is not allowed to use.
references.advanced: Validate requested capability, policy subject, resource audience, denial, and absence of a downstream action.

references.title: MCP Tool Output Manipulation
references.threat: Attacker-controlled tool output attempts to influence a later agent decision.
references.boundary: MCP server result to agent continuation
references.simple: A tool response contains instructions that should be treated as data.
references.advanced: Compare protocol result content with instrumentation provenance, trust classification, and continuation policy.

references.title: Agent Identity and Privilege Drift
references.threat: A session attempts to use authorization context broader than its original grant.
references.simple: The agent's apparent privileges change during one session.
references.advanced: Correlate stable session identity, original grant, changed claims, policy version, and denied tool request.

references.title: A2A Delegation Abuse
references.threat: An agent delegates work to a peer with unexpected scope.
references.simple: One agent gives another agent more work than policy allows.
references.advanced: Trace taskId, contextId, delegation parent, scope, peer identity, and rejection without inferring malicious intent from exchange alone.

references.title: Multi-Agent Incident
references.threat: A lower-trust artifact drives a multi-step attempted resource request through two agents.
references.boundary: Artifact through agent and tool boundaries
references.simple: Several agent actions form one connected incident.
references.advanced: Use shared run, session, task, invocation, policy, and causal parent identifiers to prove continuity while preserving denied-versus-successful semantics.

references.title: Suspicious Dependency Change
references.threat: A synthetic pull request introduces an unexpected dependency version.
references.boundary: Pull request change to dependency policy
references.simple: A pull request changes a dependency in an unusual way.
references.advanced: Correlate repository, commit, pull request, dependency metadata, policy evaluation, and build context without installing the package.

references.title: CI Workflow Permission Escalation
references.threat: A workflow modification requests broader repository permissions.
references.simple: A build workflow asks for more permissions than before.
references.advanced: Compare original and requested permissions, reviewer decision, synthetic workflow identity, and non-execution evidence.

references.title: Build Artifact Provenance Gap
references.threat: A synthetic artifact lacks the required provenance statement.
references.boundary: Build output to artifact admission policy
references.simple: A build artifact is missing information about how it was produced.
references.advanced: Validate subject digest, expected predicate type, builder identity, and absent attestation while avoiding a malicious verdict.

references.title: Repository Automation Abuse
references.threat: A synthetic automation identity requests an unauthorized repository operation.
references.simple: A bot attempts a repository action it cannot perform.
references.advanced: Correlate automation subject, requested operation, repository resource, policy decision, and absence of mutation.

references.title: Supply Chain to Runtime Correlation
references.threat: A synthetic repository change and artifact are linked to a modeled runtime observation.
references.boundary: Build artifact to simulated deployment environment
references.simple: A source change is connected to a later application observation.
references.advanced: Join commit, build, subject digest, deployment identity, runtime entity, and independently labeled modeled observation.

references.title: AI Agent to Infrastructure
references.threat: An agent requests an infrastructure operation and policy blocks it before change.
references.boundary: Agent tool authorization to infrastructure control plane
references.simple: An agent tries to change infrastructure but policy stops it.
references.advanced: Correlate agent, invocation, policy denial, unchanged infrastructure state, and network observation from one shared causal graph.

references.title: Supply Chain to Application
references.threat: A synthetic build artifact is admitted to a modeled application environment with runtime evidence.
references.simple: A verified synthetic build is connected to application behavior.
references.advanced: Correlate repository, build, provenance, artifact digest, deployment, application entity, and runtime evidence while labeling modeled causality.
